chapter: Chapter 6. Solids and the solid–liquid transition
title: The mechanism of plastic deformation

prose.text:
Atoms are tiny particles that make up materials.
An atom is the basic particle of a chemical element, a substance made from one kind of atom.

In a crystal, particles are arranged in a repeating pattern.
Deformation means a change in a material's size or shape.

A load is a push or pull applied to the material.
Strain describes a change in size compared with the original size.

When the load produces only a small strain within the elastic range, the atoms shift slightly from their usual average positions.
These are called equilibrium positions.

The atoms still move around them.
The distances between atoms and their arrangement change slightly.

Elastic deformation means that the material can recover its original size and shape after the push or pull stops.
The atoms can then return approximately to their original average positions, provided that no damage or other irreversible change has occurred.

An irreversible change does not undo itself when the load is removed.
Plastic deformation differs from this recovery: it leaves a permanent change in shape.
prose.source_text: 晶体弹性形变时，原子彼此只有很小的移动.

prose.text:
As plastic deformation builds up, the relative shifts of atoms or molecules in a crystal can reach many times their original spacing.
The crystal remains deformed after the load is removed.

A crystal lattice is the repeating pattern of particle positions.
A crystal plane is a flat layer within that repeating arrangement.
Slip means that parts of the crystal shift past one another along particular crystal planes.

When plastic deformation occurs mainly through slip, without breaking the crystal or changing its type of structure, most of the crystal can retain its ordered arrangement.
Retaining this crystalline structure does not mean that every atom keeps its original neighbors or that the lattice contains no defects, places where the pattern is imperfect.
A crystal that has undergone plastic deformation is not completely unchanged.
prose.source_text: 当塑性形变时，原子或分子的位移可以超过它们之间距离很多倍. 然而，没有破坏物体的晶体结构.

prose.text:
The original textbook explains plastic deformation in terms of slip between layers of the crystal lattice.
A single crystal is one crystal, rather than many small crystals joined together.

Tension is a pull that stretches the crystal.
Slip marks can appear on its surface under tension, as in Figure 91 a.

Stress describes force per unit area in the material.
The stress caused by pulling can tend to make neighboring parts slide past one another.

This sliding tendency is called shear.
Along suitable crystal planes and directions, shear can help slip occur.

Figure 91 b shows the relative offset between lattice layers after slip, with Latin letters used consistently to label the panels.
This is a simplified lattice model of the result of slip.
The model does not mean that complete atomic layers in real crystals necessarily move simultaneously as rigid units.

A dislocation is a line where the crystal's repeating arrangement does not fit perfectly.
As a dislocation moves, nearby particles rearrange in small steps, allowing one part of the crystal to shift past another.
Slip in real crystals often occurs through this gradual, local motion of dislocations.
prose.source_text: 晶体点阵的各个层相对稍微滑动. 受到拉伸的单晶体如图91 а 所示. 可以很明显地看到各层滑动的痕迹. 各层滑动的过程如图91 б 所示.

prose.text:
The original textbook emphasizes that slip can begin locally, rather than occurring throughout the crystal's entire volume at the same time.
The textbook uses local groups of irregularly arranged atoms in the lattice to illustrate possible starting sites.

In real crystals, dislocations and other local structures affect how slip begins and spreads.
This illustration does not mean that all plastic deformation must begin in the same kind of "weaker group of atoms".

Different defects have different effects: some structures help local slip, while others obstruct dislocation motion.
The presence of defects therefore does not always make the entire crystal easier to deform plastically.
prose.source_text: 所有的晶体原子层的滑动是在个别部分开始，而不是在整个晶体的所有体积中，它们是在由于某种原因晶格点阵强度很小的地方开始. 例如，在点阵中可以有排列紊乱的个别原子群.

prose.text:
A polycrystal consists of many grains, each a small crystal.
When plastic deformation occurs mainly through slip, slip can occur inside individual grains.

It need not begin in all grains at once.
Some grains can still respond elastically while others slip.

Different grains usually have different orientations, meaning that their repeating patterns face different ways.
The planes and directions along which slip occurs most easily therefore also differ.

A grain boundary is the place where two grains meet.
As a grain changes shape, it must still fit against its neighbors.
Grain boundaries can hinder slip.

For this reason, more stress may be needed before permanent deformation starts.
The original textbook explains that the stress needed to begin plastic deformation in a polycrystal can be greater than in a single crystal.
It notes that this extra stress is more noticeable in fine-grained materials, which are made of smaller grains.

This comparison concerns suitable slip conditions for the material, with temperature and loading conditions kept comparable.
It is not a universal rule that any polycrystal is harder to deform than a single crystal of any orientation.

Grain orientations are not necessarily completely random.
What the material is made of, which way its grain patterns face after processing, its temperature, and how it is pushed or pulled also affect the result.
A material cannot be judged solely by whether it is polycrystalline or fine-grained.
prose.source_text: 多晶体塑性形变时，在单个小晶体中，也发生点阵各层的滑动. 但是，在不同的晶体中，最容易滑动的方向是不同的，因为它们总是相对紊乱的. 因此，多晶体的塑性形变是在比单晶体更大的应力下开始，在微粒结构的材料中特别明显.

data.chapter: 第六章 固体和固-液转变
data.title: 塑性形变的机构

prose.text: 晶体弹性形变时，原子彼此只有很小的移动.
当塑性形变时，原子或分子的位移可以超过它们之间距离很多倍. 然而，没有破坏物体的晶体结构.
晶体点阵的各个层相对稍微滑动. 受到拉伸的单晶体如图91 а 所示. 可以很明显地看到各层滑动的痕迹. 各层滑动的过程如图91 б 所示.
所有的晶体原子层的滑动是在个别部分开始，而不是在整个晶体的所有体积中，它们是在由于某种原因晶格点阵强度很小的地方开始. 例如，在点阵中可以有排列紊乱的个别原子群.
多晶体塑性形变时，在单个小晶体中，也发生点阵各层的滑动. 但是，在不同的晶体中，最容易滑动的方向是不同的，因为它们总是相对紊乱的. 因此，多晶体的塑性形变是在比单晶体更大的应力下开始，在微粒结构的材料中特别明显.
